title: A Teenager Wins the Big Tennis Final
summary: Mirra Andreeva is 19 years old. She plays tennis. Last Sunday, she won the WTA Finals in California. She beat Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 in the final. She is the youngest player to win this event in 22 years. The last teenager to do it was Maria Sharapova in 2004, when she was 17. Andreeva did not lose a set all week. She lost only 26 games in five matches. She is now number two in the world. She was very nervous before the tournament. She said she had a little breakdown in practice because she was so stressed. But once she started playing, she was brave. She beat three of the world's top ten players, including Aryna Sabalenka. Against Svitolina, she lost her lead three times. Each time, she fought back. After the win, she thanked herself in her speech, just like she did when she won the French Open. She said the whole week was just a dream.
why_it_matters: Her story shows kids that nerves are normal, and fighting back can lead to big wins.
